problem.text: The new helper addresses optional profiling: its docstring specifies making @profile a no-op when kernprof has not injected it.

reasoning.text: Importing profile_opt installs an identity decorator in builtins only if profile is absent. An existing binding is preserved, and the module exports that binding as profile.
Using builtins enables bare @profile decorators without importing profile into each module's globals. The tradeoff is a process-wide binding rather than a module-local fallback.

impact.text: Six modules import the helper: generator, job, custom sampler, attention, block-sparse MLP and transformer. These imports activate its initialization; the diff adds no profiling decorators or changes to their computational methods.

source_notes.text: Whole-parent-tree search for profile found no existing Python profiling decorator or helper usage; matches were comments, build-script profiler references and calibration text. This does not exclude external instrumentation.

The parent entry read describes the preceding routing optimization and records a conditional all-expert fused-buffer mismatch. This task only adds a module-level import to that file; inspection shows its routing cardinality, fused guard and buffer allocations remain unchanged.

Issue #12, “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions,” concerns chat mode selection. Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” concerns conversion and tokenizer truncation. Their inferred connection here is only shared traceback paths—job.py and attention/transformer files—not evidence motivating this profiling utility.

limitations: No package import, kernprof integration, GPU execution or performance measurement was performed. The standalone check executed a transcription of the new helper, not the repository implementation.
The helper's stated kernprof injection convention was not independently verified against eligible profiler documentation.

claims.text: The helper and its six imports work together: imports establish the fallback before subsequent definitions can use bare @profile. The fallback returns the original function rather than introducing a wrapper, while an already injected profiler remains available.

A standard-library transcription passed checks for fallback function identity, bare-decorator name resolution and preservation of a preexisting profile binding. These checks establish those isolated Python semantics, not profiler integration.

annotation.summary: Adds an optional profiling helper and imports it in six runtime modules; absent profiling instrumentation becomes an identity decorator, without adding active profiling sites.

argv:
import builtins
src='import builtins\nif not hasattr(builtins, "profile"):\n    def _noop(func):\n        return func\n    builtins.profile = _noop\nprofile = builtins.profile\n__all__ = ["profile"]\n'
saved=getattr(builtins,'profile',None); had=hasattr(builtins,'profile')
try:
 if had: del builtins.profile
 ns={}; exec(src,ns)
 def f(x): return x+1
 assert ns['profile'](f) is f
 d={}; exec('@profile\ndef g(): return 7',d); assert d['g']()==7
 sentinel=lambda fn: ('wrapped',fn)
 builtins.profile=sentinel
 ns2={};exec(src,ns2);assert ns2['profile'] is sentinel
 print('Transcribed helper: identity fallback, bare decorator lookup, existing binding preservation passed')
finally:
 if had: builtins.profile=saved
 elif hasattr(builtins,'profile'): del builtins.profile
